title: Tiny Animals Build Earth Massive Stone Fortresses
description: Discover the incredible secret life of the tiny creatures that build our planet's largest living structures. From a microscopic partnership to a synchronized underwater blizzard, witness how coral reefs are engineered from nothing.
instagram_caption: The largest structures on Earth aren't made by humans, but by tiny, squishy creatures barely larger than a grain of rice. Subscribe to find out how they do it.

segments.narration: The largest structures on Earth built by living things aren't made by humans, but by tiny, squishy creatures barely larger than a grain of rice.
Yet, against all odds, on a single night under a full moon, the entire reef releases billions of eggs and sperm in a massive, synchronized underwater blizzard of life.
As these new larvae settle, they build directly on top of the skeletons of their ancestors, piling stone upon stone over thousands of years to craft bustling underwater metropolises.
These living fortresses protect our coastlines and shelter a quarter of all marine life. Subscribe to The Wild Mechanics for more.
